title: Multi-FPGA Synchronization and Data Communication for Quantum Control and Measurement
problem: Practical quantum computers with thousands of qubits require scalable control systems with nanosecond-scale clock synchronization and low-latency data communication within hundreds of nanoseconds. Most open-source solutions are limited to single-board RFSoC implementations, while commercial multi-FPGA solutions are prohibitively expensive.
motivation: Building practical quantum computers with thousands of qubits requires precise, synchronized, and scalable control and measurement systems.
method: The system synchronizes multiple FPGAs using a simplified version of Precision Time Protocol (PTP), which keeps their clocks aligned to nanosecond precision. For fast communication between the FPGAs, it uses Aurora protocol, a high-speed serial standard that keeps data transfer delays under hundreds of nanoseconds. These synchronization and communication layers are integrated with QubiC, an open-source quantum control and measurement system, to create a complete, scalable solution for controlling thousands of qubits across multiple FPGA boards.
key_novelty: It combines a simplified Precision Time Protocol for synchronizing multiple FPGA clocks to nanosecond precision with Aurora protocol for low-latency data communication, enabling a practical multi-FPGA quantum control system.
contributions: Scalable clock synchronization framework for multi-FPGA systems using minimal Precision Time Protocol
Low-latency data communication framework for mid-circuit measurement using Aurora protocol
Integration with open-source QubiC quantum control and measurement system
Practical multi-FPGA solution addressing gap between expensive commercial and limited open-source options

metrics.other: nanosecond-scale clock synchronization, hundreds of nanoseconds communication latency

limitations: Paper does not discuss limitations of the proposed approach.
